senses.gloss: m. (תָּאַב) desire, appetite; לת׳ to satisfy the appetite.
units: <cite ref="Chullin 84a:18-19">Ḥull. 84ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 14:26">Deut. XIV, 26</cite>, <cite ref="V00015"><he>תאוה</he></cite>) <he>למדה … אלא לת׳</he> the Torah here teaches a sanitary rule, that man should not eat meat unless he has special appetite for it; <cite ref="Tosefta Arakhin 4:26">Tosef. Arakh. IV, 26</cite>.

<cite ref="Pesachim 120a:1">Pes. 120ᵃ</cite> (in Chald. dict.) <he>דקאכיל לת׳</he> when he eats with appetite (when he begins the meal); a. e.—Esp. (with ref. to forbidden food) <he>לת׳</he> on account of an irresistible appetite, opp. <he>להכעיס</he>, v. <cite ref="M00525"><he>מוּמָר</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 27a:8">Snh. 27ᵃ</cite> <he>מומר … לת׳</he> a non-conformist who eats unslaughtered meat merely to satisfy his appetite (because it is cheaper than the slaughtered, Rashi); a. fr.
